Market Outlook
11Remark  1_Information as of 12 May 2026
Sources  Drewry | Linerlytica  | Sea -Intelligence | S&P Global Market Intelligence | Bloomberg | XenetaSupply -Demand Dynamics
•Structural Oversupply : Global fleet growth 
at ~8.9% ( Clarksons /Linerlytica ) due to record 
newbuilding deliveries.
•Effective Capacity: 15–18% of global supply 
remains absorbed by Red Sea rerouting 
and slow -steaming (Sea -Intelligence).
•Demand Recovery : Moderate growth of 2.0 –
2.8%;  Intra -Asia remains the primary 
growth driver.
Freight Rate Trends
•Volatile Stabilization:  Rates have retreated 
from 2025 peaks but remain above 2019 levels.
•Cost Pressure:  Higher operational floors due 
to bunker costs and EU ETS  carbon taxes.
•Contract Market:  Shifting toward shorter-
term flexibility as shippers hedge against future supply influx.Operational & Regulatory Landscape
•Decarbonization:  Full EU ETS  implementation and IMO CII ratings are now one 
of the cost drivers.
•Network Stability:  Reliability stabilizing at ~65% ; port congestion persists in 
key Asian hubs .
Middle East Geopolitical
Current Landscape: Sustained Volatility & Strategic Realignments
•Regional Instability:
•Protracted tensions in Gaza continue to drive friction across the “Axis of 
Resistance. ”
•Periodic escalations on the Israel- Lebanon border and in Iraq/Syria 
maintain a high -risk environment for regional stability.
•Maritime & Supply Chain Risks:  continued rerouting of vessels around the 
Cape of Good Hope >> higher transit costs, increased insurance premiums, and 
extended lead times.
•Geopolitical Balancing:  Gulf monarchies prioritize domestic economic 
transformation (e.g., Vision 2030).
•Market Impact:  The " Middle East Risk Premium " persists in energy and 
shipping markets. Supply chains must remain agile to navigate sudden disruptions to trade arteries and fluctuations in oil volatility.
